questions.explanation: Errors here usually come from swapping in a claim the position rejects. Divine command theory identifies moral rightness with conformity to God's commands. This is the position defended by William of Ockham. The claim that divine command theory identifies rightness with independently existing moral facts is a common mistake about the view, often described as "misses the dependence of morality on command". A fair assessment also has to reckon with this worry: the Euthyphro dilemma. The distinction between the view and its caricature is what the question tests.
